recommendations.title: `## What is deliberately not enforced` in `ROADMAP_FORMAT.md` (step 3 "Write ROADMAP_FORMAT.md specifying both artifacts
recommendations.body: `## What is deliberately not enforced` in `ROADMAP_FORMAT.md` (step 3 "Write ROADMAP_FORMAT.md specifying both artifacts and naming the code that enforces them") states the verb "exits non-zero only when it fails to finish — a stage that exhausts its retry budget without clearing its gates", naming only the `_RC_INCOMPLETE = 1` path; `cmd_roadmap` also returns `_RC_USAGE = 2` for every pre-flight failure `run_roadmap` raises `RoadmapError` / `RoadmapArtifactError` for — an unreadable brief, an out-of-range `--from-stage`, a missing prompt template, a malformed upstream artifact, or an upstream artifact failing its own stage's gates. An operator or CI treating rc as "0 or budget-exhaustion" misreads a usage failure as a model failure, and this bullet is the doc's only account of exit codes
recommendations.suggested_action: in `ROADMAP_FORMAT.md`'s `## What is deliberately not enforced`, replace the single-cause appositive with both classes — a stage that exhausts its retry budget, and a pre-flight failure that stops the run before any stage is invoked

recommendations.title: The "A hand edit is judged exactly like model output" bullet in `ROADMAP_FORMAT.md`'s `## What is deliberately not enfor
recommendations.body: The "A hand edit is judged exactly like model output" bullet in `ROADMAP_FORMAT.md`'s `## What is deliberately not enforced` says `--from-stage N` "re-reads each artifact from disk and re-runs it through its own stage's gate set", but `plan_tool/roadmap.py:_load_and_regate_below` re-reads and re-gates only the stages *below* N — every stage from N up is re-invoked and its artifact overwritten. The bullet also calls the result of a broken edit "a violation naming the row" without saying that path raises `RoadmapError` and halts **before any Claude call**, which contradicts the doc's own `### What a violation is for` claim that violations are retry text that blocks a stage. The doc's own example — deleting an entity a constraint anchors to — trips `check_entity_references` during that pre-flight load, so the reader is pointed at the one channel the doc never describes
recommendations.suggested_action: scope the sentence in `ROADMAP_FORMAT.md` to the stages below N and state that a below-N gate failure halts pre-flight rather than feeding a retry
